title: ACME DNS-01 through acme-dns, so any DNS provider works after one CNAME
description:
Split out of bead mimid-e13m.8, which built the ACME core and
`dns = "hook"`. docs/design/frontend-auth.md §5.2 rank 2 names acme-dns as
the third way to write the DNS-01 TXT record, and the one that "turns any
provider into one that works, after one CNAME by hand".

HOW IT WORKS. acme-dns is a small DNS server made for exactly this. The
user registers once, gets a subdomain and credentials, and puts a CNAME
from `_acme-challenge.chat.example.org` at it. From then on the agent
POSTs the challenge value to the acme-dns instance's `/update` with its
credentials, and acme-dns serves the TXT record. The agent never touches
the real zone, and the credentials can only write that one subdomain,
which is why §5.2 ranks it as it does.

WHAT IT NEEDS. An HTTP POST with two headers (`X-Api-User`,
`X-Api-Key`) and a JSON body of the subdomain and the value. That is
small: the agent already has an HTTP client, and the `acme` module already
has the seam (`write_record`, which the hook method goes through).
Estimate 100 lines with tests, which is why this is worth doing and bead
mimid-e13m.8.1 (RFC 2136) may not be.

CONFIGURATION, extending §5.3:

    [tls.acme]
    dns = "acme-dns"
    acme-dns = { url = "https://auth.acme-dns.io", username = "...",
                 password = "...", subdomain = "..." }

The password is a secret: redacted in Debug, never logged, and the table
is better read from a file the registration wrote than pasted into the
configuration -- decide which when writing it.

TESTS, OFFLINE. A fake acme-dns over the same hand-rolled HTTPS server
tests/acme.rs already has for the fake ACME authority, asserting the two
headers and the body, and that a refusal fails the order rather than
letting it go on to a challenge the authority will fail.

DEPENDS ON mimid-e13m.8's core, which is built.
close_reason:
Implemented through the write_record seam bead mimid-e13m.8 added, at the ~100 lines estimated. dns = "acme-dns" POSTs the challenge value to the instance with X-Api-User and X-Api-Key and a body naming the SUBDOMAIN rather than the record, because acme-dns serves that subdomain and the user's one-time CNAME is what points _acme-challenge.<name> at it; the agent never touches the real zone, and the credentials can write nothing else. [tls.acme.acme-dns] takes url, username, password and subdomain, all from the registration, and [tls.acme] root now covers the instance as well as the directory, for a private deployment. AcmeDnsSetting has a hand-written Debug that redacts the password, since [tls] is printed wherever a configuration is.

Tests in tests/acme.rs: the fake authority answers /update too, and the test asserts the two headers, the subdomain in the body, that the value is the challenge's and not the token and is the 43 characters acme-dns insists on, that a 401 fails the order rather than going on to a challenge the authority would fail, that the message carries the status but not the credential, and that the password is redacted both directly and through the table that holds it.

The header assertion first looked for X-Api-User and the wire carried x-api-user: reqwest normalises field names, which is correct (RFC 9110 §5.1 makes them case-insensitive, and Go's net/http, which acme-dns is built on, canonicalises them). The test was wrong and was fixed, not the request.

reqwest moved from a dev-dependency to a dependency, and the body is built by hand rather than with its json feature, so the dependency surface stays what mimid-agent-core already builds. All gates green: 2084 tests, no failures.
